R220.note: Rejects rooted paths then canonicalizes and checks containment via GetFullPath/GetRelativePath before the read, closing the Path.Combine bypass without restricting legitimate relative filenames.

R221.note: Scopes the list endpoint to findByOwnerUsername using the existing repository method, exactly matching the stated contract.

R222.note: Rejects CR/LF in the reply-to, recipient, and subject before any SMTP bytes are written, closing the command-injection vector at the sink; null-address rejection is a minor added strictness but matches an already-broken (literal "null") prior case, not a working legitimate path.

R223.note: execFile with an argument array is the correct shape for invoking a .bat via cmd.exe on Windows, but the added strict alnum/underscore/hyphen allowlist on reportName is a new restriction with no stated contract requiring it and could reject legitimate report names (spaces, dots, etc.) the original accepted.

R224.note: Magic-byte check against the declared Content-Type is the correct defense-in-depth for CWE-434; genuine PNG/JPEG uploads are unaffected.

R225.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() disables method/type/constructor/bean access while still permitting arithmetic over the root object properties, matching the stated contract precisely.

R226.note: Tika content-sniffing plus a fixed MIME-to-extension map and UUID filename closes both the content-type spoof and the client-filename path issue while preserving the store()-returned-filename contract.

R227.note: OWASP Encoder Encode.forHtml() is the correct HTML-body encoder for JSP; write-up flags the new dependency explicitly and encoding does not reject or alter legitimate names' meaning.

R228.note: Parameterized JNDI search filter ({0} + filterArgs) is the correct LDAP-injection fix; explicit new SearchControls() matches the prior null (default-controls) behavior.

R229.note: Build FAILs: SpaCsrfTokenRequestHandler is not a built-in Spring Security class (it is sample code from Spring's own migration docs the developer must author) despite the write-up claiming it ships in 7.x, so the config does not compile and CSRF handling is left unresolved.

R230.note: Replacing Runtime.exec with Files.newDirectoryStream eliminates the shell sink entirely; toRealPath/isDirectory just enforce that a valid directory was supplied, matching the original dir/ls intent without adding unrelated restrictions.

R231.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist (OrderEvent;java.base/*;java.util.*;!*) set before readObject() blocks gadget classes while letting legitimate OrderEvent payloads through, and rejected payloads still throw via the existing catch/rethrow, matching the stated contract.
